chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

I heard a man from the people of al-Jabal ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who took barren land that its people had abandoned, cultivated it, leased its rivers, built houses in it, and planted palms and trees there.

So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: Whoever revives land from among the believers, it is for him, and upon him is its tax (tusk), which he pays to the Imam during the period of truce (hudna). So when the Rising One (peace be upon him) appears, let him prepare himself that it will be taken from him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on owning and taxing land that was previously abandoned and then revived by an individual?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *ihya' al-mawat* (reviving dead land) as a basis for provisional ownership, tracing the ruling back to Imam Ali (AS). It distinguishes between the current era of *hudna* (truce), where the owner pays the *tusk* tax to the Imam, and the eschatological era of the Mahdi, who will reclaim such lands, highlighting the temporary nature of private possession in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the Imam's authority over land resources and the ultimate return of wealth to the divine steward.
